au.footer: codes made on your device · sealed with a passphrase of their own · on every device you sign in on
au.setupText: Your two-factor secrets are kept in your account, so every device you sign in on has them, sealed with this passphrase. Without it nobody can read them: not the relays, not the hub, not even someone who learns your account’s password.
au.setupHint: At least {n} characters; a few words are easy to remember and hard to guess. It cannot be recovered: if you forget it, the codes in here are lost, so keep a backup (in the settings).
au.syncedAccount: Kept in your account, on every device you sign in on.
au.syncedKey: You are using this device’s own key: the codes stay on this device until you create an account.
au.lockedText: They are sealed with a passphrase of their own, not your account’s password.
au.lockedElsewhere: The passphrase was changed on another device: enter the new one.
au.empty: No accounts yet. Add one with the QR code a service shows when you turn on two-factor sign-in.
au.tapToCopy: Tap a code to copy it.
au.deleteText: Its codes are gone from all your devices. Turn off two-factor sign-in at the service first, or keep another way in, or you may lock yourself out.
au.qrWarning: This QR code holds the secret: whoever scans it gets the same codes. Show it only to move the account to another authenticator.
au.notAnAccount: That is neither a two-factor secret nor an otpauth:// link.
au.noQr: No QR code found in that picture.
au.foundHint: If the service asks for a code to finish setting up, enter this one.
au.pictureText: A screenshot or a photo of the QR code.
au.textLabel: Or paste the link or the secret
au.noCamera: The camera is not available here: allow it for this site, or use a picture.
au.cameraHint: Hold the QR code in front of the camera.
au.how.1: Two-factor codes (TOTP, RFC 6238) are made on your device from a secret and the time; no server is asked.
au.how.2: A backup file is your vault as it is, still sealed with its passphrase; a list of links is not sealed at all.
au.settings.lockAfter: Lock again when the page has been away for
au.settings.lockText: This choice is for this device. Closing the page locks the codes at once.
au.settings.passText: A new passphrase seals your codes anew; your other devices then ask for it.
au.settings.backupText: A backup file is your vault as it is, sealed with the passphrase it has now. A list of links opens in any authenticator app, unsealed.
au.settings.importText: Import takes a backup file (with its passphrase) or a text file of otpauth:// links; accounts already here are skipped.
au.settings.nothingFound: Nothing to import in that file.
au.settings.plainText: The file holds every secret in plain text: whoever has it has your codes. Use it to move to another app, then delete it.
au.settings.removeHint: When the passphrase is lost: removes the vault and every account in it from your account, so you can start again.
au.settings.removeText: Every account in it is gone from all your devices. Sign-ins that need its codes will need another way in.
